Shares are this community’s count divided by the Port Moody total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Heritage Woods PM
Heritage Woods is a board (MLS) sub-area of the City of Port Moody — the eastern part of the Heritage Mountain grouping on the city's north shore.
Streets, schools and getting around Heritage Woods PM

items.t: Where condo stock concentrates: there is no apartment-condo shelf to concentrate. — listing counts (SnapStats, September 2026)

Schools: Heritage Woods Secondary School at 1300 David Avenue is the area's landmark public building (SD43); an SD43 School Locator run for that address returned Heritage Mountain Elementary, Eagle Mountain Middle and Heritage Woods Secondary. Catchments are address-based — confirm any specific address in the locator.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Heritage Woods PM

items.t: Creek and slope rules that bite on this hillside: lots with a watercourse need a riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 setbacks, and environmentally sensitive and steep slope development permit areas can apply. No floodplain or ALR land was confirmed in Heritage Woods.

blocks.text: Good to know about Heritage Woods PM

items.t: The OCP protects this hillside's character on paper. Chapter 14, Section 14.3 policies for the Heritage Mountain grouping aim to retain the existing residential and forested character — a reason no seniors tower or care campus is planned for this sub-area in the OCP (now Bylaw 2026, No. 3522).

Port Moody's seniors-housing action is all happening down the hill. Council declined a Kyle Seniors Housing proposal at second reading on Oct 14, 2025 (5-1), then directed staff to investigate affordable seniors housing opportunities — all Moody Centre items, with nothing proposed for Heritage Woods.

Kyle Centre, the older-adult hub serving the city, is being replaced. The 1977 Kyle Centre at 125 Kyle Street is at end of life; its redevelopment's first phase — conceptual design for a proposed 39,000 sq ft facility, plaza and expanded Kyle Park — began in summer 2025, funded with $515,000 from the Community Amenity Contribution Reserve, with room kept for potential future affordable housing at the west end of the City-owned lands under a separate project.
Cobalt Sky's published facts disagree with each other. Neither figure should be quoted in a listing — the strata plan BCS2068 and the Form B are the settlement documents.
Commuting: David Avenue runs both ways, into Coquitlam and into Port Moody; the routes are compared on the
Heritage Woods neighbourhood page

A single house listing here was flagged "Senior Community: No." MLS data carried in a current Heritage Woods rental listing (119 Aspenwood Dr) explicitly records "Senior Community, No" for the property — a small, concrete example of the sub-area's non-seniors character in the board's own data.

Quest at Heritage Woods — 2200 Panorama Drive. Strata townhouse — counted once, here

The fresh verification landing here (Nov 2, 2026): a current listing records a unit at 2200 Panorama Drive as Type Townhouse, built 2005, with strata fees of $592/mo, in Heritage Woods PM; a second current listing records Sub-Type Row / Townhouse, built 2005, naming "The highly sought after Quest at Heritage Woods"; current complex listings describe "Quest at Heritage Woods, a wonderful family-oriented community surrounded by nature," with a playground. No age restriction stated — general-market, not 55+.

Transit: TransLink buses serve the north shore and connect to Moody Centre Station and Coquitlam Central Station.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Heritage Woods PM

items.t: Form B diligence (every counted strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

City zoning and SSMUH: Zoning Bylaw No. 2937 puts single-detached homes in RS zones and multi-residential homes in RT and RM zones; small-scale multi-unit housing, including coach houses and accessory dwelling units, is permitted in RS and RT zones outside the transit-oriented areas. Hillside diligence: lots with a watercourse need a riparian assessment and Zoning Bylaw Section 5.4 setbacks, and environmentally sensitive and steep-slope development permit areas can apply. No floodplain or ALR land was confirmed in Heritage Woods.

Port Moody property taxes: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on outstanding amounts after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 15, 2026; utilities are billed separately (2026 utility bill due February 27, 2026). This staged 5% + 5% is Port Moody's own municipal scheme as the City publishes it — it is not the Mission flat-10% regime and not the rural Taxation (Rural Area) Act regime.

blocks.text: Heritage Woods home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

21 townhomes sold in Heritage Woods with a median price of $1,158,000 (the middle half sold between $997,000 and $1,280,000), taking a median of 16 days to sell at 98.3% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $631 per square foot, a median year built of 2004 and a median strata fee of $469 a month.
